dsh-lesson-loop
Guard denials, gate failures and human thumb-downs become project lessons; only a rule a human confi
rmed is injected back into the model at session start.
**A self-evolution loop for dsh: one lesson bus the guard plugins report to, one rule library a huma

##  What it does
- **One bus, no coupling.** Sibling plugins report through the optional `lessonLoop` service; a prof
ile without this package only drops those reports. The host half provides the service, the client ha

lf renders a web card holding the switches and the rule review desk.
- **Sink.** Each report appends
one line to the event stream and merges into a candidate card keyed by (project, category, signatur

e); at `promoteThreshold` that key is marked ready for review.
- **A machine never promotes a rule.*
* Status `armed` is only ever a human decision — the card's `arm` action writes it, and the startup
migration merely carries an existing armed state onto a merged card. `reject` / `demote` / `archive`

/ `edit` / `revive` are human actions too.
- **Remind.** A project-agnostic standing section keeps
the loop visible, and each root session receives the full text of its project's armed rules at `agen

t/created`. Subagent sessions are skipped.
- **Zero model tools, zero HTTP routes of its own.** The
card's data plane is the official Typert Remote namespace `lessonLoopRules`, reached through the hos
is the official Typert Remote namespace `lessonLoopRules`, reached through the host `/api` gateway.
### How a rule is judged
- Three counters answer three different questions: `violation` (the scenario fired and was broken),
`suppressed` (the scenario fired and was followed, driven by `pass`), `samples` (the rule was presen

t and not violated).
- The only ratio is `violation / (violation + suppressed)`; `samples` is exposu

re and never a denominator.
- `samples` counts a durable session once even when it is resumed: dupli

cate disposal edges are deduplicated, so reopening a session does not inflate exposure.
- Demotion n
eeds a positive `suppressed`, `violation` at `demoteThreshold`, real evidence at `demoteMinSamples`,

and the ratio at `demoteRatio`.
- A rule with zero clean hits whose scenario keeps firing is **unde
terminable**: neither the ratio nor the decay can retire it, so it stays armed for a human. One `pas
er the ratio nor the decay can retire it, so it stays armed for a human. One `pass` clears the flag.
##  Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Remove with `dsh plugin --profile web remove @jayyuen66/dsh-lesson-loop`. The package is on the publ
ic npm registry, so installation needs no credentials.
- **Node.js `>= 24.9`, host `dsh` on the rolling `^0.2.1-rc.5 || ^0.2.2-alpha.3` window.** The plugi
n's own floor is `engines.node` (`>=24.9.0`), which is the host's floor from `0.2.2-alpha.2` up: a h
ost below it never starts, so a lower claim here would promise an environment nobody can install int
o. The requirement the host reads is `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.1-rc.5 || ^0.2.2-alpha.3`), and it **decid
es alone** — with that field present, `evaluatePluginCompatibility` never looks at the `@deepseek-ai
/dsh*` peers. Measured: `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-rc.1` and `0.2.1-rc.3` are refused, `0.2.1-rc.5` throug
h `0.2.2-rc.1` pass, `0.3.0` is refused. The support window rolls: this package is verified against
every released host version inside the window at publish time and re-verified once the window moves,

so the version number in this bullet is not a standing promise.
[该节后续省略]
##  What it does not provide
- **No model tools.** There is no `lesson_report` tool; the surface is the service plus the card's n

amespace.
- **No HTTP route of its own.** Authentication, Host / DNS-rebinding / Origin checks and b

ody limits are the host gateway's.
- **No CLI subcommand.** The only command it contributes is the i

n-session `/lessons-digest`.
- **No outbound request of its own.** The distillation call goes throug

h the host `llm` service.
- **No self-re-enabling rules.** A `rejected` card may return to `candidat
e` at the revive threshold; only a human can arm it again.
##  Data and privacy
| Aspect               | Content
| Written to disk      | The event stream at `$DSH_HOME/cache/lesson-loop/events.jsonl` (a discardab
le derived-data location) plus its transient `.lock` / `.tmp` siblings, and the `rules` array in the

`lesson-loop` section of the settings document          |
| Network              | No call of its o
wn. `/lessons-digest` sends this session's negative feedback and the project's recent lessons to the
current default model through the host `llm` service, so that content leaves the machine when that

model is remote |
| Retention            | The event stream keeps details and rule statements in ful
l, with zero truncation; `maxLessonsBytes` is a disk fuse, not a context cap

|
| Evidence convergence
| Rule-card `evidence` is the one exception: an over-long detail is truncated with an ellipsis and o
nly the most recent rows per card are kept, at write time only. `signature` and the counters are nev

er trimmed                        |
| Concurrency          | Rule-library writes carry cross-process
CAS; event-stream appends share one lock with trimming

|
| Lan
guage             | Host-side wording follows the official locale preference; stored rule statements
are user data and are never rewritten
